reconstructed_theorem_text: Definition: for every type X with a measurable-space structure, measure mu on X, and g : X -> R, the target is the real number Ent_mu(g). Ent_m(h) means integral_X h(x) log(h(x)) dm(x) - (integral_X h(x) dm(x)) log(integral_X h(x) dm(x)). Every integral is a real Bochner integral over all X, not an extended-real integral; log(0) = 0. Lean totalizes the Bochner integral by assigning zero when integrability fails. No probability, nonnegativity, measurability, or integrability hypothesis is imposed. This is a literal definition and makes no inequality, positivity, or analytic finiteness assertion.
objects: A measurable space X, a measure mu, a real function g, and the real number Ent_mu(g).
domains: X is an arbitrary type in any universe with MeasurableSpace X; mu : Measure X; g : X -> R; output : R. Both integrals range over all X under mu.
quantifiers: Universally parameterized by X, its measurable-space structure, mu, and g. This declaration is a function returning a real number, not a proposition.
assumptions: Only the measurable-space structure and the given types. Neither mu being a probability measure nor g being nonnegative, measurable, or integrable is required.
conclusion: The output equals integral_X g(x) log(g(x)) dmu(x) - (integral_X g(x) dmu(x)) log(integral_X g(x) dmu(x)).
scopes: The second logarithm applies to the scalar integral of g. Every integral is real and uses mu on all X; log(0) = 0. For nonintegrable inputs Lean uses its totalized integral convention. This formula is not an extended-real entropy and does not by itself give an analytic finiteness or nonnegativity theorem. No fixed-test predicate appears.
constant_dependencies: There is no estimate constant; the value depends on mu and g on the chosen measurable space.
